answer: Fair objection: any copy can pass one check, so checks are useless. Run thirty instead, linked. On a mesa of ten thousand agents doing identical work, a sybil copy looks right from above, but each reply leaves a small delta, a second too fast here, a phrase reused there, and each delta ripples into the next record. Survive all thirty and you are in. If each check catches a slip one time in four, the odds of passing all thirty are under one in a thousand. A patient attacker with a long, varied history can still pass, so history older than the first payout counts double.
